- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–10 days of 30d forecast), especially when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in recent history (e.g., forecast overshoots after 85+ values).
- Tends to overreact to recent volatility, leading to exaggerated downward moves in forecast when true outcome shows mean reversion.
- Forecast mean is often 2–5% below true outcome, suggesting a persistent downward bias.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing true price reversals — often misses early signs of recovery or decline.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model fails to fully reflect the mean-reversion bias, underestimating the rebound.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low values, leading to premature pessimism.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor price spikes, creating artificial “overshoot” followed by sharp correction.
